case_prompt:
A 49-year-old male who had undergone orthotopic liver transplantation approximately nine months earlier was admitted to the hospital with a one-week history of recurrent episodes of abnormal temperature regulation and hypothermia.

On physical examination upon admission, he was clinically stable without localized abdominal tenderness or acute peritoneal signs.

Admission laboratory evaluation demonstrated leukocytosis with a white blood cell count of 16.17 x 10^9/L (reference range: 3.5-9.5 x 10^9/L). The peripheral differential revealed profound hypereosinophilia with an eosinophil percentage of 60.90% (reference range: 0.4-8.0%) and a relative neutropenia with a neutrophil percentage of 30.90% (reference range: 40-75%).

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered given fever, leukocytosis, and subsequent rise of inflammatory markers (CRP 61.8 mg/L, procalcitonin 0.85 ng/mL, IL-6 48 pg/mL) in an immunosuppressed liver transplant recipient, but ruled out by complete lack of response to broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotic coverage.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Despite several days of antibiotic treatment (Cefoperazone Sodium and Sulbactam Sodium, 1.5 g, Q8H), the laboratory examination on August 11 showed elevated C-reactive protein of 61.815 mg/L (CRP; normal, <10 mg/L), procalcitonin (Pct) of 0.85 ng/mL, and IL6 of 48 pg/mL (normal, 0-7 mg/mL).

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Acute Allograft Rejection / Drug-Induced Hypereosinophilic Syndrome
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered due to profound peripheral blood hypereosinophilia (60.90%) in an allograft recipient on immunosuppressive therapy, but ruled out by direct pathogen identification and mechanical parasite recovery rather than immunological rejection.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: while CDC did not report a positive trematode IGg until four days later... On August 21, many Clonorchis Sinensis worms were flushed out of the biliary tract

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Prompted by profound peripheral hypereosinophilia (60.9%) and refractory fevers despite antibiotics; confirmed by plasma metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) identifying 60 Clonorchis sinensis sequence reads, subsequent CDC trematode IgG positivity, and macroscopic visualization of numerous adult flukes flushed from the biliary tree during biliary drainage, leading to full clinical and hematologic normalization following oral praziquantel.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: To determine the cause of the fever, mNGS was performed, and the next day's sequencing data showed 60 clonorchis sinensis sequences, while CDC did not report a positive trematode IGg until four days later. The patient was prescribed praziquantel (0.2 g, Tid) orally for 3 consecutive days from August 14 to 16 and from August 31 to September 2, respectively. On August 21, many Clonorchis Sinensis worms were flushed out of the biliary tract (Figure 5A). Subsequently, all blood indicators of the patient returned to normal
